newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen firm after Fed keeps rate steady.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen firm after Fed keeps rate steady.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to firm on Wednesday after Wall Street stocks surged after the U.S. Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged at Tuesday's closely watched policy-setting meeting, brokers said.
But the market is still cautious about currency movements, which have been volatile recently, they said.
On Tuesday, the Nikkei average fell 156.92 points or 0.77 percent to close at 20,332.83. Nikkei June futures fell 210 points to 20,340.

"The yen might stabilise after the Fed left rates unchanged, but export-oriented shares might not be able to gain much ground because their domestic (currency) rate is above 120 yen," said a broker at a second-tier Japanese securities house.
"Investors will remain interested in issues driven by domestic demand, especially NTT (Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp)," he said.
The dollar was standing at 113.16/26 yen at 2330 GMT, recovering from a low of just below 112 yen on Tuesday in Tokyo.
Brokers also said shares in the financial sector were dragged down by a widening of a scandal surrounding Nomura Securities Co Ltd after prosecutors raided Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd on Tuesday.
Electronics giant Sony Corp was down 80 yen at 9,650, while Toyota Motor Corp was 60 yen weaker at 3,520 and Honda Motor Co Ltd 110 yen lower at 3,520.
The dollar was trading at 114.20/30 yen as of 0243 GMT, off a low of 111.98 yen marked on Tuesday.
The stock market remained wary of movements in the currency market, even after the U.S. Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged at Tuesday's closely watched policy-setting meeting.
The Fed's decision buoyed Wall Street stocks, and the Dow Jones industrial average gained more than one percent to close 75 higher at 7,303 on Tuesday.
Another reason for the weakness in the domestic stock market was the financial sector, brokers said.

Shares in DKB were down by 40 yen at 1,350 at midday, after being ask-only at the opening. "As long as concerns over the Japanese financial sector are not wiped out completely, the Nikkei 225 index cannot head strongly upwards," said a broker at one of the "Big Four" securities houses.
By sector, decliners were led by rubber, railway/bus, automobiles, pharmaceuticals, and pulp/paper.
The major gainers were gas, sea transport, and land transport. - Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
